subject: Medilink request: extended net terms + weekly invoicing alignment
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medilink.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T16:12:00+01:00
Subject: Request: extended net terms + staggered weekly invoicing

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product fits a few of our upcoming workflows really well. Finance asked me to reach out with a commercial ask so we can get procurement moving. High level:

- Medilink would like to request Net60 for the first 3 months of the pilot (volume expected to be low, ramping after month two).
- We prefer weekly invoices (every Monday) rather than monthly — it aligns with our internal cost-centres and helps chargeback to clinics.
- We are a UK-headquartered entity; we'll need to confirm VAT alignment. Could you confirm what VAT evidence you need and whether Redwood can issue invoices net of VAT for our UK subsidiary?

Two practical notes: our treasury has a Friday payment cutoff for ACH/GBP rails; if we can keep invoices dated early in the week we can meet the Net60 target more predictably.

I can share a temp PO to unblock pilots. Attaching a placeholder PO.

Thanks,
Oliver
Finance Ops
Medilink Health

Attachment: Medilink_PO_Temp_12345.pdf (pdf)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medilink.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended net terms + staggered weekly invoicing

Hi Oliver — appreciate the clear ask and the PO stub. Looping in Ben (Finance) and Marissa (Legal) to keep this moving.

Quick response / our starting position:

- We can support weekly invoicing (Mon/Wed cycle) to align to your treasury cutoffs, but weekly invoices increase operational load and our minimum billing increments. To offset that, we propose Net45 for the pilot period rather than Net60.

- Conditional credit cap: we can grant an initial credit corridor of GBP 150,000 (cumulative outstanding) for the first 90 days, subject to on-time payment and receipt of VAT registration evidence. If payments are clean we will automatically increase the cap after 90 days.

- VAT: please send your UK VAT registration certificate (or UK subsidiary VAT number). To issue invoices net of VAT we need the valid VAT number on file and a signed tax form (we've attached our Redwood VAT evidence checklist).

- FX / currency: if invoices are sent in GBP but paid via a USD bank, we ask to agree on the FX date (invoice date vs payment date) and a 0.5% FX buffer to cover short-term conversion variance. Ben, can you confirm how we should model that operationally?

- PO referencing: we can accept a temp PO for onboarding but require a final PO number or SOW reference before volume crosses GBP 50k.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Oliver: share VAT certificate + confirm preferred invoice day (Mon or Wed)
2) Ben: confirm operational mechanics for weekly invoices + FX buffer
3) Marissa: draft a short-term amendment (pilot addendum) with the conditional cap and payment terms

Attaching: Draft_Payment_Terms_Proposal.pdf, Redwood_VAT_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if useful.

Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

Attachments: Draft_Payment_Terms_Proposal.pdf (pdf), Redwood_VAT_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medilink.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Medilink Finance <finance@medilink.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T08:09:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended net terms + staggered weekly invoicing

Camila — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide the UK VAT registration cert by end of day Monday.
- Preferred invoice day: Monday works best (gives our AP team time to queue before Friday treasury cutoff).
- Regarding Net45 vs Net60: the business really prefers Net60 for the pilot window to preserve working capital; would Redwood consider Net60 if we agree to an early-payment program (1% discount if paid within 10 days)? That would keep costs predictable for us and reduce your receivable days if you take the discount.
- PO: we will provide a formal PO number as soon as procurement clears the pilot SOW (should be next week).

Also attaching the placeholder PO and a short note on our treasury rails.

If Ben or Marissa want to jump on a 20-min call to iron the FX buffer and cap mechanics, happy to schedule Thursday morning UK time.

Best,
Oliver

Attachment: Medilink_PO_Temp_12345.pdf (pdf)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Medilink request: decision points and asked items

Ben / Marissa — forwarding the thread. Key decision points for ops/legal: please see highlighted action items below.

Summary / asks:
- Medilink will provide VAT cert by Monday and prefers Monday invoices.
- They are asking to stretch to Net60 but offered an early-pay 1% discount within 10 days. We previously proposed Net45 + conditional GBP 150k cap.
- We need a short pilot amendment (30–90 day pilot language) that:
  * Lists the conditional credit corridor (GBP 150,000) and the auto-increase clause after 90 days of on-time payment
  * Defines weekly invoice cadence and invoice day (Monday)
  * Specifies FX handling (invoice currency, FX date, 0.5% operational buffer) and who bears conversion fees
  * Includes an optional early-payment discount (1% if paid within 10 days) and how discounts are applied against outstanding balance

Operational questions for you, Ben:
- Can we process weekly invoice batches with our current AR tool (and tag them to Medilink cost-centres)? If not, what's the lead time?
- How do we apply the early-pay discount in billing and reporting (credit vs cash reduction)?

Marissa: please draft a 1-page pilot addendum that covers above points and a fallback to standard Net30 after the pilot if no final contract is in place. Also need a quick clause authorizing us to suspend weekly invoices and revert to monthly if operational burden becomes material.

I plan to respond to Oliver once I have your inputs and a short draft amendment. Thinking of proposing the following paths to them to keep momentum:
A) Net45 + no discount + GBP150k cap (fastest for us)
B) Net60 + 1% early-pay discount + GBP100k cap (middle ground)
C) Net30 + invoice automation + no cap change (fallback)

Happy to take calls to finalize.

Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
